title: Navigation Prism: task-hubs + route-matrix prototype for console IA
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Redesign the Redwood Console primary navigation using a 'Navigation Prism' concept: surface contextual task-hubs (grouped by intent) and a route-matrix that supports deep-linking, fast workspace switching, and quick access to rollouts and cost insights. This ticket covers wireframes, mid-fidelity prototypes, eng/pm reviews, and a handoff-ready Figma file.
background: Current console nav is a mix of role-specific items and monolithic left-rail links. Users report cognitive load when switching between dashboards, rollout controls, and cost breakdowns. As feature surface grows (Dedicated, Private, Optimize), we need a scalable IA that preserves discoverability and reduces clicks to key tasks.
goals: Reduce average clicks to open a per-route dashboard from 4 -> 2
Provide one consistent path for rollouts and A/B toggles regardless of workspace type
Expose cost breakdowns and token-level views within two interactions from the global nav
Support deep-linking and URL-driven routing for bookmarks and API-driven navigation
constraints: Must work within existing Console header height and not increase vertical footprint
Left rail needs compact mode for small viewports and long route lists
Engineering runtime must support per-route telemetry hooks; avoid heavy client-side route computation
Role/permission awareness: some hubs should surface differently for read-only vs admin roles
proposed_solution: Introduce a multi-layer nav pattern: (1) Global prism (top-left) that switches primary intent hubs (Observe, Serve, Manage, Billing), (2) Task-hub rail that shows grouped tasks and contextual quick actions, (3) Route-matrix overlay for power-users that surfaces flattened routes and keyboard shortcuts. Workspace switcher becomes an inline micro-panel with recent-workspaces + tenant-aware suggestions. Inline rollouts and cost-summary cards are previewable in the rail via hover/peek.
alternatives_considered: Keep existing left-rail but add nested accordions — rejected due to discoverability and long-scroll issues
Floating quick-actions popover on topnav — rejected because it didn’t scale for role-based controls and context
Horizontal megamenu with grouped links — rejected due to screen real-estate and mobile constraints
review_comments: PM - Aisha Kapoor (2025-02-21): prefer 'Observe' hub over 'Monitor' to align with docs; prioritize rollout entry points for Dedicated customers.
Eng - Daniel Chen (2025-02-24): implement route-matrix as server-provided flattened route table to avoid client recompute; routing library changes required.
Security - Priya Nair (2025-02-26): workspace switcher micro-panel must enforce tenant isolation and hide links when user lacks permission to view resource metadata.
Design critique - Emma Novak (2025-03-01): hover peek is helpful but needs friction to prevent accidental reveals on trackpad; recommend 200ms delay and persistent open on keyboard focus.
decisions: Adopt 'Navigation Prism' naming and four primary hubs: Observe, Serve, Manage, Billing
Route-matrix will be a server-side endpoint that returns user-scoped flattened routes with metadata
Workspace switcher becomes an inline micro-panel with MRU (most recently used) + suggestions; removed global modal approach
Cost preview cards will show top-3 line items in rail hover and link to full cost view
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates hub switch and task-hub rail for all four hubs
Engineer sign-off on route-matrix API contract exists (PR link in attachments)
Accessibility: keyboard navigation for hub switcher and rail, aria labels present
Performance: no >40ms added time for initial console paint in compact nav mode
PM acceptance test: end-to-end path to open a rollout and view cost breakdown within two interactions
